title: Princess Samantha and the Sock Monster
author: Dady Fredy
subtitle: A Bedtime Story by Dady Fredy
dedication: For Samantha — the bravest, kindest princess in the whole pink castle.

lines: Samantha the Brave, with her crown on her head,
Never gives up till the monster's in bed!
closing: Samantha the Brave, with her crown on her head,

pages.title: Princess Samantha and the Sock Monster
pages.subtitle: A Bedtime Story by Dady Fredy
pages.dedication: For Samantha — the bravest, kindest princess in the whole pink castle.

lines: In a little pink castle, when day turned to night,
Princess Samantha was tucked in just right.
Her bunny named Button lay snug by her head,
With his floppy pink ears on her soft pillow-bed.
Then Dady came in for a goodnight kiss —
"Sweet dreams, my princess, my sweet little miss!"
But just as he turned off the lamp with a click,
The closet door creaked… and it opened up quick!
Out tumbled a monster, all lumpy and tall,
Made of all the lost socks, from the big to the small!
There were stripy ones, spotty ones, woolly and grey,
And one pink sock with hearts on — its nose, by the way!
"I'm the SOCK MONSTER!" it rumbled. "Hooray!
I'm taking your Dady to Sock Land today!"
It wrapped Dady Fredy in socks head to toe,
Then WHOOSH through the closet — and off they did go!
Samantha sat up. Did she cry? Did she hide?
NO! She put on her crown, with her bunny beside.
"Don't worry," said Button, with a wiggle and hop,
"We'll get Dady back, and we never will stop!"
Through the closet they tiptoed, past coats and past shoes,
Into Sock Land — a land of all colors and hues!
There were sock-trees and sock-hills and a sock-river too,
And little sock-birdies that sang "Sock-a-doo!"
They hopped over mountains of slippers and lace,
Till they found the Sock Monster — with tears on its face!
It sat all alone on a big woolly stone,
And Dady was stuck on a stripy sock-throne.
"Why are you crying?" Samantha asked, kind.
The monster sniffed, "My best sock friend I can't find!
I'm a sock with no partner — I'm one, not a pair,
So I took someone's Dady to have someone there."
Samantha thought hard — then Button said, "LOOK!"
And he pointed his paw at a dark little nook.
There, curled up and sleepy, all cozy and bright,
Was a pink sock with hearts — and it matched it just right!
She carried it over and held it up high:
"Here's your missing sock-partner! No more need to cry!"
The monster went quiet… then wiggled with glee,
"My partner! My pair! Oh, how happy I'll be!"
"I'm sorry I took him. I just felt alone.
Now I've found my best sock — so go on, take him home!"
It unwrapped Dady Fredy, so gentle and slow,
Then hugged them both close with its pink heart-sock nose.
Back through the closet, past coats and past shoes,
They hurried, all three, with no time to lose.
Then Dady tucked her in and squeezed her up tight:
"My brave little princess — you saved me tonight!"
"You didn't use swords, and you didn't use might —
You were clever and kind, and you made it all right.
The bravest of hearts doesn't roar or attack,
It helps a lost friend find their way back."
So if ever your sock goes missing one day,
Don't worry — it's gone off to Sock Land to play.
It's keeping the Sock Monster company there,
So nobody, ever, is missing a pair.
Now Button is yawning, the moon's glowing pink,
And Samantha's eyes close in a slow, sleepy blink.
Goodnight, little princess, so brave and so true…
Sweet dreams — and the Sock Monster says goodnight too.
Goodnight, Samantha.
Goodnight, anak.
